summary:
A1 (longitudinal curves) is done in the worktree, nothing committed. The hull builds as one hollowed solid, and every longitudinal curve is now a single cubic B-spline fitted to the measured points. That removes the 7300 step, the bow S-bend, the 91 mm forefoot step and all np.interp kinks, and every curve stays within 12.5 mm of its data. Max beam is held at exactly 2680.0 mm. The spline code is pure numpy (de Boor plus a least-squares fit with an active set for shape constraints), so the repo gets no scipy dependency.

What each curve is fitted to:
- **Deck line:** least-squares spline through deck_halfbreadth.csv (x<7300) and STERN_OUTLINE (weight 10). It is required to curve outward everywhere (no inflection) and to stay at or below BEAM/2. Aft of the transom corner the hold segment still continues from the spline end.
- **Sheer:** smoothing spline through DECK_EDGE_Z, lam = 4e7.
- **Strake:** least-squares spline through strake_z_mm, constrained to bend one way only.
- **Profile (bottom_z):** one spline from stem head to transom, bending one way only. It runs through the V9 stem formula for x<=850, the traced uw_station.csv forefoot and canoe bottom from 1008 to 2800, and a new table CANOE_BOTTOM_HIDDEN where the keel, propeller and rudder hide the bottom. That table holds V9 values, with the tail past 7650 smoothed to remove a V9 kink at 7800 that came from _fair's end effect. The fit is pinned exactly at the stem head (= sheer), at (LWL_FWD, 0) and at the keel-root x, so root_z is unchanged.
- **_table:** natural cubic spline, which is C2, for both SECTION_FULLNESS and WATERPLANE. A smooth curve through the old aft WATERPLANE points bulges up to 80 mm outside V9, so I moved the aft points (0.85–1.00) to cut the old corners instead. The 7239 hinge is gone. fullness and wl_half_breadth keep their names and signatures for A2.

I also had to change section_inner, which is not in my list. With the new, shallower forefoot, its centreline cut took the first crossing of an offset loop, which put a zero-width fold in the void near x≈1128. The first build had 7174 non-manifold STL edges and 12k degenerate triangles there. It now cuts at the last crossing; only 6 sections near x 1076–1140 change.

Side effect outside my scope: the coachroof's 45° step-wedge cut, which used to silently do nothing (edges-1), now works because the planform moved slightly. The front now rises from the deck at x≈2225 to the roof at about 2320 instead of standing as a vertical wall at 2200.

Visually, the forefoot outline and the stern quarter are cleaner in close-up renders. At full-model scale the difference is modest: the DWL crease and the hollow topsides come from section(), which is A2's job.

changes.what: Removed _load, _fair and the np.interp curve tables. Added numpy-only splines: _Spline (de Boor), _basis, _bending (the integral of s''^2), _fit (weighted least squares with curvature penalty, one-way-bending constraint, equality points and upper bounds, solved with an active set) and _read. deck_half_breadth is one spline through the trace and STERN_OUTLINE: no inflection, max = BEAM/2, and the hold past 7891 runs from the spline end via _stern_table (same name and behaviour). sheer_z is a smoothing spline (P.SHEER_SMOOTHING). strake_z is a least-squares spline bending one way only. bottom_z is one spline from stem head to transom, pinned at the stem head, (LWL_FWD, 0) and the keel-root x. _table is a cached natural cubic spline. _BW_MAX now comes from the spline maximum. section_inner cuts at the centreline at the last crossing instead of the first (fixes a zero-width fold at the forefoot). Module docstring rewritten. Comments in Norwegian with oe/aa, CRLF kept.

New SHEER_SMOOTHING = 4.0e7 right after DECK_EDGE_Z. New CANOE_BOTTOM_HIDDEN table (22 points, 3250-7950) right after KEEL_FILLET: canoe bottom where keel, propeller and rudder hide it, V9 values with the tail from 7650 smoothed. WATERPLANE aft points changed from (0.85 0.97)(0.93 0.88)(1.00 0.56) to (0.85 0.96)(0.90 0.90)(0.95 0.765)(1.00 0.525), with an explanatory comment. Comment on SECTION_FULLNESS updated. DECK_CAMBER line and every other value unchanged.

measurements:
CURVES vs MEASURED POINTS (full-scale mm), V9 -> V10:
- Deck half-breadth vs the deck_halfbreadth.csv trace: max 13.5 -> 11.6 mm. The 11.6 is at x=2616, in the known dent-then-bump zone 2516-3220; elsewhere 8.9.
- Deck vs STERN_OUTLINE: 0 -> 4.3 mm.
- Deck step at 7300: +9.48 -> 0.00 mm.
- Deck plan-curvature sign changes over 0-7891: 8 -> 0 (bow S-bend gone).
- Deck beam: 2681.0 -> 2680.0 mm.
- Deck, V10 minus V9: -4.3 to +12.5 mm. The +12.5 is at x=300, where the bow moves back out onto the trace.
- Sheer vs DECK_EDGE_Z: max 7.1 -> 5.0 mm; inflections 4 -> 2; largest kink 0.99 -> 0.003 deg.
- Strake vs strake_z_mm: max 2.0 -> 1.3 mm; curvature sign changes 7 -> 0.
- Profile vs uw_station trace, 1008-2800: max 85.5 -> 10.3 mm. The 10.3 is at x=1655, where the bottom bridges a small dent in the trace.
- Profile step at 1008: -91.1 -> 0.0 mm; largest kink 81 -> 0.03 deg; sign changes 8 -> 0.
- Stem vs the V9 stem formula: within -3.8 to +11.0 mm over 0-850; +12.7 at x=900, where V9 flattens to horizontal at the DWL against a traced slope of -0.53.
- DWL crossing at x=1008.0. Keel root bottom_z(4590): -501.42 -> -501.40.
- Transom bottom on the centreline: (7769, -252.2) -> (7770, -248.8). Stem head: bottom_z(0) = sheer_z(0) = 1204.2.
- WL half-breadth: largest kink 26.9 deg at 7239 -> 0.045 deg; WL inside the deck everywhere with at least 38 mm margin. SECTION_FULLNESS: slope steps -> C2.
- Speed: 80,000 curve calls take 0.1 s.

BUILD (python build_hull_only.py ... 0.05 0.01 abs 40):
- Builds and hollows as one solid; build log reports shell plastic 230 cm3 (baseline 228).
- STL a1_v10.stl: 855,478 triangles, 42.8 MB, 103 non-manifold edges (baseline_fine 124), volume 228.9 cm3 (baseline 228.6).
- Bounding box 266.0 x 89.3 x 104.8 model mm (baseline 266.0 x 89.4 x 104.8), so the bed fit is unchanged.

SILHOUETTES vs baseline_fine.stl (exact plane sections every 6 mm, full scale):
- Plan: max 8.4 mm at x=4008, p95 7.6 mm; aft of 7300 between -7.3 and -2.0 mm.
- Profile top: +1 to +4 mm along the sheer. The exception is x 2205-2320, where the coachroof front is now sloped (up to 133 mm at x≈2205).
- Profile bottom:
  - 0-1008: -4.3 to +7.9 mm
  - 1300-2000: -33.4 to -4.8 mm (now on the trace)
  - 2000-2800: -14.5 to +18.3 mm
  - 2800-3400: +18.5 to +27.1 mm (bridge into the hidden keel zone)
  - 3400-5800: -0.2 to +26.9 mm
  - 5800-7300: 0 to +1.6 mm
  - 7300-7770: -6.2 to +2.7 mm
open_issues: section_inner (curves.py, A2's area) was changed to cut the centreline at the last crossing. Without it, the new shallower forefoot gave a zero-width fold in the bow void, with 7174 non-manifold edges and 12k degenerate triangles. A2 should keep this or an equivalent when it replaces section().

Side effect: the coachroof's step-wedge cut (deckhouse.py), which silently did nothing in V9 (edges-1), now cuts because the deck planform moved a few mm. The front now slopes from x≈2225 at the deck to 2320 at the roof instead of a vertical wall at 2200. This matches the drawing but depends on a fragile boolean; package C should build the slope into the roof profile.

uw_station.csv aft of the keel is not used. 6050-6450 is the propeller. The flat line at -437 to -444 from 6450 to 7450 does not match the photos (IMG_9374, IMG_9387 show the canoe body rising steadily toward the transom). The aft bottom keeps the V9 shape via CANOE_BOTTOM_HIDDEN. If that flat line really is the canoe bottom, the aft bottom is 30-108 mm too high; only the original drawing can settle it.

Out of scope (keel): the model keel's leading edge meets the canoe body at x≈3790, because the root wire sits 260 mm inside the hull with LE at 3380. The traced LE leaves the hull at about 3000-3380 with a large root fillet and is at x≈4000 at z=-1150, where the model is at ≈4570. This is a large visible difference from the photos.

The canoe bottom between the traced forefoot (to 2800) and the hidden keel zone is now 18-27 mm higher than V9 at 2800-3800 (unmeasured zone, keel-fillet region). The stem is up to 12.7 mm above the V9 stem formula at x≈900, where that formula flattened unphysically to horizontal at the DWL.

WATERPLANE aft: the corner-cut points make the DWL up to 60 mm narrower than V9 at x≈7239 and at most 5 mm wider anywhere (sections-3 says the aft WL is over-full). The plan curvature has two same-sign peaks (≈7040 and ≈7640), no inflection. The clamp at t=1.015 (x≈7808, behind the transom at the DWL) still breaks the slope, as in V9. A2 may make the WL an output anyway.
The STL still has 103 non-manifold edges from tessellation (baseline 124), 71 of them at the forefoot centreline near the DWL. They are not a regression, but a slicer may report them.

Viewed as a whole model, the visible change from A1 alone is modest. The main robot causes (DWL crease and hollow topsides in section(), relative STL tolerance in build.py, sharp edges) belong to A2, D and B/C. The curvature fixes will show more clearly once those land.
This took about twice the 60-minute target, mostly from three ~3-minute builds and from tracking down the forefoot void fold.
